newsitem.title: PERU: Beeper used to alert Peruvian hostages of raid.
newsitem.headline: Beeper used to alert Peruvian hostages of raid.

text.p: Peru's security forces alerted hostages of their planned rescue at the Japanese ambassador's home by a personal beeper message to a captive just before their explosive assault, military sources said on Wednedsay.

Minutes before elite commandos burst into the mansion, the armed forces sent a message to retired naval officer Luis Giampietri Rojas, who had apparently kept his beeper despite checks by the Tupac Amaru hostage-takers, the sources said.

Freed hostages confirmed they then passed around word of the imminent assault among themselves on the upper floor of the two- storey building while Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels played soccer in a reception room below.
When a fellow hostage sidled up to Father Juan Julio Wicht to warn him he was about to be freed, the Jesuit priest said he thought it was just another joke to ease the tension.

But President Alberto Fujimori said the warning was vital to the success of the operation as the 72 hostages reacted calmly during the first explosions when commandos stormed into the residence and battled with the heavily-armed guerrillas.
All 14 hostage-takers, one hostage and two commandos died in Tuesday's attack that received worldwide praise for its meticulous planning and execution by 140 elite troops.
